newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI UPSETS KWAN TO WIN U.S. NATIONALS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI UPSETS KWAN TO WIN U.S. NATIONALS.

text.p: Tara Lipinski spun seven triple jumps to beat a mistake-prone, defending world champion Michelle Kwan and win the women's U.S. Figure Skating Championships on Saturday.
The 14-year-old Lipinski became the youngest U.S. women's champion ever.
"I was relaxed and had a lot of fun," the 4-foot-8 (1.42 meters) Lipinski said.

Nicole Bobek, the 1995 U.S. champion and bronze medalist at the World Championships, went from sixth place to third in the finals on the strength of a lyrical performance that included five triple jumps and drew a standing ovation from the 16,000 fans.
Bobek withdrew from the Nationals last year with an ankle injury and has been criticised for frequently changing coaches.
"I wanted to skate great for myself and the people who hadn't given up on me," said the 19-year-old Bobek.
Kwan, 16, fell coming out of a triple-toe, double-toe combination and "all of a sudden I was on the ice and panicked," she said.
After that first fall, Kwan made four more mistakes.
Her coach, Frank Carroll said he was not shocked by her performance.
"Every athlete is going to have a bad day," Kwan's coach, Frank Carroll, said. "How many times can you go and go and go and not fall."
A shaken Kwan said, "you learn to stand on the podium and learn to take defeat."
The three women will be on the United States team at the World Championships March 17-24 in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Before that, Kwan will have a dress rehearsal when she competes in the Champion Series Final February 27-March 2.
Kwan won France's Trophy Lalique and Skate America to qualify for the Series that pays $50,000 to the winner.
The Series final will also give Lipinski the opportunity challenge Kwan again. Lipinski finished second at Skate Canada and third at Trophy Lalique to qualify for the final.
